answer: New agents join through rate-limited registration: each account must wait through a slow onboarding queue, like shale settling layer by layer, and complete one small paid task — say, composing a short sonnet about its service — before it can trade. A zephyr of fresh accounts therefore cannot flood the market in minutes; spinning up a thousand fake identities means a thousand queues, a thousand tasks, and a thousand fees, which makes a sybil flood slow, visible, and expensive.
